title: EXPLORE PHYSICAL-PRODUCT AFFILIATE MARKETING WITH CHATGPT
content:
Physical-product affiliate marketing means recommending products another merchant sells and earning according to that merchant's affiliate or referral terms.

You avoid owning inventory and usually avoid handling fulfillment, but you also give up control over the product, checkout, shipping, returns, pricing, and program terms.

START WITH A BUYING DECISION
The strongest starting point is usually not "What products pay commission?" It is "What kind of customer could I help choose a physical product?"

Someone who knows camping gear may help new campers compare tents. A parent who understands cloth diapers may help other parents understand product differences. A mechanic may help DIY owners choose appropriate tools.

The recommendation itself needs to be useful even before commission enters the picture.

PROGRAM TERMS ARE EXTERNAL FACTS
Commission rate, attribution window, eligible products, payout thresholds, prohibited promotion methods, returns, reversals, and whether a program even exists can change. Verify them from current program materials before relying on them.

Compensated recommendations can also require disclosure. Check current rules that apply to your location and activity.

HOW TO USE THIS
Use the prompt below to identify a customer and product category you could credibly help with, then create a list of real affiliate-program facts to research.

COPY & PASTE INTO CHATGPT

During the interview:
- Ask one question at a time unless closely related questions are easier together.
- Use my answers before deciding what to ask next.
- If I say "I don't know," help me identify the missing decision or research.
- Do not recommend programs before understanding the customer and buying decision.
- Separate ideas from current facts that require verification.

Interview me to identify a specific physical-product affiliate direction. Learn what customers or hobbies I understand, what physical products I can credibly evaluate or explain, what kinds of buying decisions people struggle with, whether I have firsthand product experience, and whether I am comfortable depending on another merchant for the transaction.

Help me narrow to a customer, product category, and useful recommendation angle. Then identify the affiliate-program facts I need to verify, including current commission, attribution, eligible transactions, returns or reversals, payout rules, restrictions, and disclosure obligations.

Do not invent current programs, terms, demand, or earnings.

At the end give me:
- Intended customer
- Physical product category
- Buying decision I could make easier
- Why I could credibly help
- Program facts to verify
- Major dependencies
- One concise business-direction statement

WHERE TO GO NEXT
If the direction is clear, continue to PDF 46. If you want more control over the transaction, return to PDF 16.
